data.narrative:
Quantum Brilliance is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised $50M+ to date. The broader quantum computing sector comprises 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method here. Using total raised ($50M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $100M. A peer-median approach is not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing space; while 8 private-sector peers exist, none meet the narrow filter criteria for direct comparison, and a broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $115M (high), with a median point of $100M. This range reflects reliance on a single methodological anchor—stage-progression—which introduces material model risk. The principal uncertainty is the absence of tightly comparable Series A quantum companies, limiting cross-validation. Additional validation would benefit from closer examination of capital efficiency and technology differentiation relative to the named peer set, data not present in the current dataset.
